questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines& $\dfrac{x + 2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2}$~and~$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{0}$& is&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{x + 2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2}$

$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{0}$

Now we know that,

Shortest distance between two skew lines is given by,

$SD = \left|\left(\overset{→}{a2} - \overset{→}{a1}\right)\left(\overset{→}{n1} \times \overset{→}{n2}\right)\left|\overset{→}{n1} \times \overset{→}{n2}\right|\right|$

Now finding,~$\overset{→}{n1} \times \overset{→}{n2} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{n1} \times \overset{→}{n2} = - 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

And~$\overset{→}{a2} - \overset{→}{a1} = \left(4\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k} - \left(- 2\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)\right) = 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

Now putting the value in formula we get,

$SD = \left|\dfrac{\left(6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}\right)\left(- 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right)}{16 + 16 + 4}\right|$

$⇒ SD = \left|\dfrac{- 24 + 2 - 32}{6}\right| = \dfrac{54}{6} = 9$

questions.q: If the mirror image of the point $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$ in the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1}$ is  \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right),$ then $14\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)$ is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given point is $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$.

Let, $Q \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right) be the image of $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$ and $' O '$ be the mid-point of $PQ$ which is on the given line

\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1} = \lambda (say)

$⇒ x = 3\lambda + 1, y = 2\lambda - 1, z = \lambda + 2$

let \left(3\lambda + 1, 2\lambda - 1, \lambda + 2\right)$ be the co-ordinates of $O$.

Direction ratios of the line is ${a}_{1} = 3, {b}_{1} = 2, {c}_{1} = 1$

Also, direction ratios of $PO$ are

\left(3\lambda - 2, 2\lambda - 5, \lambda - 7\right)$

As, $PO$ is perpendicular to the line

$3\left(3\lambda - 2\right) + 2\left(2\lambda - 5\right) + \lambda - 7 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda - 23 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = $\dfrac{23}{14}

$∴O$ point is \left(3 \cdot $\dfrac{23}{14} +$1, 2 \cdot $\dfrac{23}{14} -$1, $\dfrac{23}{14} +$2\right)$

Since, $O$ is mid-point of $PQ$

$∴ \left(3 \cdot $\dfrac{23}{14} +$1, 2 \cdot $\dfrac{23}{14} -$1, $\dfrac{23}{14} +$2\right) = \left(\dfrac{3 + \alpha}{2}, \dfrac{4 + \beta}{2}, \dfrac{9 + \gamma}{2}\right)

So, on comparing both side and solving we get,

\alpha = \dfrac{62}{7}, \beta = \dfrac{4}{7}, \gamma = \dfrac{- 12}{7}

Hence, 14\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) =$108$

$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{λ}$~and $\dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{4} = \dfrac{z - 5}{5}$~is $\dfrac{1}{3}$, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda$& is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, shortest& distance between two line is given by& \left|\left({a}_{2} - {a}_{1}\right) \cdot \left({b}_{1} \times {b}_{2}\right)\right| \left|{b}_{1} \times {b}_{2}\right|$

Here,~${a}_{1} = \left(1, 2, 3\right)$~${a}_{2} = \left(2, 4, 5\right)$

$\overset{→}{b}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \lambda\overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{b}2 = \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So, S.D.~$= \left|\left(\left(2 - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(4 - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(5 - 3\right)\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right)\right|\left|{b}_{1} \times {b}_{2}\right|$

Calculating~$\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 3 & \lambda \\ 1 & 4 & 5\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i} \left(15 - 4\lambda\right) + \overset{^}{j}\left(\lambda -10\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(5\right)$

$= \left(15 - 4\lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda -10\right)\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So,~\left|\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right| = $\sqrt{\left(15 - 4\lambda\right)2 + \left(\lambda - 10\right)2 + 25}

Now again,~

S.D.~$= \left| \left(\overset{^}{i} +$2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\$right)\cdot \left[\left($15 - 4\lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda -$10\right)\overset{^}{j} + 5k\right]\right|$\sqrt{\left(15 - 4\lambda\right)2 + \left(\lambda - 10\right)2 + 25}

\left|$15 - 4\lambda + 2\lambda - 20 + 10\right|$\sqrt{\left(15 - 4\lambda\right)2 + \left(\lambda - 10\right)2 + 25} = \dfrac{1}{3}

squaring~both side we get,

3\left($5 - 2\lambda\right)2 = 225 + 16{λ}^{2} - 120\lambda + {λ}^{2} + 100 - 20\lambda + 25$

$12{λ}^{2} + 75 - 60\lambda = 17{λ}^{2} - 140\lambda + 350$

$5{λ}^{2} - 80\lambda + 275 = 0$

${λ}^{2} - 16\lambda + 55 = 0$

\left(\lambda -5\right)\left(\lambda -11\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 5, 11$

So sum of~$5 + 11 = 16

questions.q: For real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta \ne 0,$~if the point of intersection of the straight lines~$\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3}$~and~$\dfrac{x - 4}{β} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3}$~lies on the plane $x + 2y - z = 8,$~then $\alpha - \beta$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3}$~and~$\dfrac{x - 4}{β} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3}$~lies on the plane $x + 2y - z = 8$.

Let~$\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3} = ∅$

and~$\dfrac{x - 4}{β} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3} = q$

Any point on the first line can be considered as \left(ϕ + \alpha, 2ϕ + 1, 3ϕ + 1\right)$

and a point on the~second line can be~\left(q\beta + 4, 3q + 6, 3q + 7\right) .$

For intersection of the lines~$ϕ + \alpha = q\beta + 4 . . . \left(1\right)$

$2ϕ + 1 = 3q + 6 . . . \left(2\right)$

$3ϕ + 1 = 3q + 7 . . . \left(3\right)$

For~ \left($2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$~$ϕ =1, q =- 1$

So, from \left($1\right)$~\alpha + \beta =$3$

Now, point of intersection is \left(\alpha +$1, 3, 4\right)$

It lies on the given plane, therefore,~\alpha +$1 + 2 \times3 - 4 = 8 ⇒ $\alpha =$5$

~$⇒ $\beta = -$2$~from~\alpha + \beta =$3$

Hence,~\alpha - \beta =$5 - \left(-$2\right) = 7$

$

questions.q: The foot of perpendicular of the point  \left(2, 0, 5\right)$~on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{5} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1}$ is  \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$. Then. Which of the following is NOT correct?
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given line is

$L: \dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{5} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1} = \lambda$ (let)

~

Let foot of perpendicular is~$P \left(2\lambda - 1, 5\lambda + 1, - \lambda - 1\right)$

$\overset{→}{PA} = \left(3 - 2\lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(5\lambda + 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(6 + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Direction ratio of line is

$\overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now,~$\overset{→}{PA} ⊥ L$, so

$\overset{→}{PA} \cdot \overset{→}{b} =0$

$⇒ 2\left(3 - 2\lambda\right) - 5\left(5\lambda + 1\right) - \left(6 + \lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ 6 - 4\lambda - 25\lambda - 5 - 6 - \lambda = 0$

$⇒ - 30\lambda - 5 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - $\dfrac{1}{6}

So,

$P \left($2\lambda - 1, 5\lambda + 1, - \lambda - 1\right) ≡ $P\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)

Now,

\alpha ==2\left(- $\dfrac{1}{6}\right) -$1 = - $\dfrac{4}{3}$⇒ \alpha = - $\dfrac{4}{3}

$\beta ==5\left(- $\dfrac{1}{6}\right) +1 = \dfrac{1}{6}⇒ $\beta = $\dfrac{1}{6}$

\gamma = - \lambda -$1 = \dfrac{1}{6} -1 ⇒ $\gamma = - $\dfrac{5}{6}$

So,

$\dfrac{β}{γ} = - \dfrac{1}{5} \ne -5$

$

so, $4\left(4\lambda - 3\right) + 2\left(2\lambda - 1\right) + 3\left(3\lambda - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

Then which one of the following points lies on the line passing through $( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$ and making angles $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ with $y -$axis and $z -$axis respectively and an acute angle with $x -$axis?
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

${L}_{1} ≡ \dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{3} = \lambda$

$⇒ M ( \lambda, 1 + 2\lambda, 2 + 3\lambda )$

$⇒ \overset{→}{PM} = \left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(1 + 2\lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda - 5\right)\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{→}{PM}$ is perpendicular to line ${L}_{1}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{PM} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{PM} . \overset{→}{b} = \left[\left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(1 + 2\lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left($3\lambda - 5\right)\overset{^}{k}\right] . \left(\overset{^}{i} +$2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \lambda - 1 + 4\lambda + 2 + 9\lambda - 15 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda = 14$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

$⇒ M = ( 1, 3, 5 )$

Now, $M$ is midpoint of $\overset{→}{P}$ and $\overset{→}{Q}$

$⇒ \left(1, 3, 5\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{1 + \alpha}{2}, \dfrac{0 + \beta}{2}, \dfrac{7 + \gamma}{2}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{1 + \alpha}{2} =$1, $\dfrac{β}{2} =$3, $\dfrac{7 + \gamma}{2} =$5$

$⇒ $\alpha =$1, $\beta =$6, $\gamma =$3$

Now, required line having direction cosine \left(l, m, n\right)$, where given $m = cos\left(\dfrac{- 2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{2}& n = cos\$left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{2}

Also, $l^{2} + m^{2} + n^{2} = 1$

$⇒ l^{2} + \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 + \left(- $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$2 = 1$

$⇒ l^{2} = $\dfrac{1}{4}

$⇒ l = $\dfrac{1}{2}

[Line make acute angle with $x -$axis]

So, the equation of line passing through \left(1, 6, 3\right)$ will be given by,

$\overset{→}{r} = ( \overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} ) + \mu \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}\right)

Option \left(3\right) \left($3, 4, 3 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)$satisfying for $\mu = 4$

$

questions.q: Let $P\text{and}Q$ be the points on the line $\dfrac{x + 3}{8} = \dfrac{y - 4}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{2}$ which are at a distance of $6$ units from the point $R ( 1, 2, 3 )$. If the centroid of the triangle $PQR$ is \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right),$ then ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} + {γ}^{2}$ is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $\dfrac{x + 3}{8} = \dfrac{y - 4}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{2} = \lambda$.

$⇒ x = 8\lambda - 3, y = 2\lambda + 4, z = 2\lambda - 1$

Let, $P ≡ \left(8\lambda - 3, 2\lambda + 4, 2\lambda - 1\right)$.

Now, given $R \left(1, 2, 3\right)$ and $PR = 6 & QR = 6$.

So, by distance formula we get,

$⇒ \left(8\lambda - 4\right)2 + \left(2\lambda + 2\right)2 + \left(2\lambda - 4\right)2 = 36$

$⇒ 64{λ}^{2} + 16 - 64\lambda + 4{λ}^{2} + 4 + 8\lambda + 4{λ}^{2} + 16 - 16\lambda = 36$

$⇒ 72{λ}^{2} - 72\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 0, 1$

$⇒ P ≡ \left(-3, 4, - 1\right)\text{and}Q ≡ \left($5, 6, 1\right)$

Hence, centroid of $△ PQR$ will be,

\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$≡ \left($1, 4, 1\right)$.

$⇒ {α}^{2} + {β}^{2} + {γ}^{2} = 18

$

Given,

questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines $x + 1 = 2y = - 12z$~and $x = y + 2 = 6z - 6$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Equation of the lines

$x + 1 = 2y = - 12z$~and $x = y + 2 = 6z - 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + 1}{1} = \dfrac{y}{12} = \dfrac{z}{- 112}$ and $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y + 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{16}$

We know that, shortest distance between the lines is given by~$S . D = \left(\overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q}\right)\left|\overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q}\right|$

Here~$\overset{→}{p} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}2 + \dfrac{- \overset{^}{k}}{12} \text{ and } \overset{→}{q} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}6$~and~$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

~$⇒ S . D = \left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q}\right)\left|\overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q}\right|$

Now solving~$\overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q} ≡ \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & \dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{- 1}{12} \\ 1 & 1 & \dfrac{1}{6}\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q} ≡ \dfrac{1}{6}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{4}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q} ≡ 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

Hence,~$S . D = \dfrac{\left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)}{{2}^{2} + {3}^{2} + {6}^{2}} = \left|\dfrac{- 14}{7}\right| = 2$

Then the distance of the mid-point of the line segment $AB$~from the plane $2x - 2y + z = 14$& is

questions.solution:
Given,

The line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{6 - y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{5}$~intersect the lines $\dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 7}{3} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1}$~ and $\dfrac{x + 3}{6} = \dfrac{3 - y}{3} = \dfrac{z - 6}{1}$ at the points $A$ and $B$ respectively,

Now plotting the diagram, we get,

Now solving,~$\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 6}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{5} = \lambda$~and~$\dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 7}{3} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1} = t$~we get,

$A ≡ ( \lambda, - 2\lambda + 6, 5\lambda - 8 ) ≡ ( 4t + 5, 3t + 7, t - 2 )$

Now comparing both side and solving we get,~$t = - 1, \lambda = 1$

Hence, point$A ( 1, 4, – 3 )$

Now solving,~$\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 6}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{5} = \mu$~and~$\dfrac{x + 3}{6} = \dfrac{y - 3}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 6}{1} = k$~we get,

For point~$B ≡ ( \mu, - 2\mu + 6, 5\mu - 8 )$~$≡ ( 6k - 3, - 3k + 3, k + 6 )$

Now comparing both side and solving we get,~$k = 1, \mu = 3$

Hence, point~$B ( 3, 0, 7 )$

So, mid-point of~$AB = M ( 2, 2, 2 )$

Now finding, distance of $M$ from the plane $2x – 2y + z – 14 = 0$~we get,

\left|\dfrac{4 - 4 + 2 - 14}{{2}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}\right| = \left|\dfrac{- 12}{3}\right| = 4$

$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines $\overset{→}{r} =  \left(- \overset{^}{i} +3\overset{^}{k}\right) + \$lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} -$a\overset{^}{j}\right)$~and $\overset{→}{r} = \left(- \overset{^}{j} +$2\overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu  \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$~is \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}},then the integral value of $a$& is equal to _____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
D.R. 's of& $\overset{→}{a}1 = \left(-1, 0, 3\right)$

D.R. 's of~$\overset{→}{a}2 = \left(0, - 1, 2\right)$

D.R. 's of~$\overset{→}{b}1 = \left(1, - a, 0\right)$~

D.R. 's of~$\overset{→}{b}2 = \left($1, - 1, 1\right)$~

Now,~$\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1 = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

and~$\overset{→}{b}1 $\times \overset{→}{b}$2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}$ \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } - a \text{ and } 0 \\ 1 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right|$

$\overset{→}{b}1 $\times \overset{→}{b2} = \overset{^}{i} \left(-$a\right) - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\left(a - 1\right)$

i.e.~\left|\overset{→}{b1} \times \overset{→}{b2}\right| = \sqrt{a^{2} + 1 + \left(a - 1\right)2}$

So,~\left(\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1\$right)\cdot \left(\overset{→}{b}$1 $\times \overset{→}{b}$2\right) = 2 - 2a$

Shortest distance between the lines,~$\dfrac{2\left(1 - a\right)}{a^{2} + 1 + \left(a - 1\right)2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

Squaring on both the sides, we get,

3\left($1 - a\right)2 = a^{2} - a + 1$

~i.e.~$a = 2, \dfrac{1}{2}$

$

questions.q: Let a line having direction ratios $1, - 4, 2$~intersect the lines~$\dfrac{x - 7}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1}$~and $\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y - 7}{3} = \dfrac{z}{1}$~at the points $A$~and $B$. Then \left(AB\right)2$ \text{ and } is equal to$

questions.solution:
Let& $A$~be~ \left(3\lambda + 7, - \lambda + 1, \lambda - 2\right)$~and~$B$~be~ \left(2\mu, 3\mu + 7, \mu\right)$

DR's~of $AB$~is

\left(3\lambda - 2\mu + 7, - \lambda - 3\mu - 6, \lambda - \mu - 2\right)$

Now,~

$\dfrac{3\lambda - 2\mu + 7}{1} = \dfrac{- \lambda - 3\mu - 6}{- 4} = \dfrac{\lambda - \mu - 2}{2}$

i.e.~$- 12\lambda + 8\mu - 28 = - \lambda - 3\mu - 6$

$⇒ \lambda = \mu - 2$

Also~

$- 2\lambda - 6\mu - 12 = - 4\lambda + 4\mu + 8$

$⇒ \lambda = 5\mu + 10$

After solving above two equations, we get~$\lambda = - 5, \mu = - 3$

i.e.~$A = \left(-8, 6, - 7\right)$~and~$B = \left(-6, - 2, - 3\right)$

Hence,~\left(AB\right)2 = 4 + 64 + 16 = 84

$
